slides.text:
Cookies are going away.

Tracking isn't going anywhere.

**Your hardware alone is enough to identify you.**

A fingerprint is a hash built from small device signals.

Your GPU, CPU, fonts and screen size each leak details.

**Enough signals combined become almost unique to you.**

Fingerprints come from two places.

Your network, and your hardware.
bullets: Network: IP and headers. Easy to change.
Hardware: GPU, CPU, memory. Surprisingly stable.
Fonts, screen size and audio add more detail.

slides.text:
Each new signal narrows down who you could be.

That idea has a name: information entropy.

**A fingerprint just needs to be rare, not unique.**

panel.small: of Americans: ZIP, birth date, sex

slides.text:
Cookies and fingerprinting both track you.

They behave nothing alike.
bullets: Cookies: a file on your device. You can delete it.
Fingerprints: built from your hardware. Nothing to delete.
Cookies need consent. Fingerprinting runs silently.

slides.text:
Privacy extensions feel like the obvious fix.

Developers in the discussion flagged a catch.

**Running one makes you rarer, which makes you easier to spot.**

Save this version, it's short enough to screenshot.

No single trick beats protection built into the browser itself.
bullets: Chrome and Edge stop at isolation, not fingerprinting
Brave, Tor and Mullvad add real protection by design

slides.text:
Which browser do you actually trust not to fingerprint you?

**Save this before you run your own test and get surprised.**
